relations.relationship: Examines unequal national agency and the use of women as symbolic bearers of national belonging.
relations.evidence_note: Primary pp. 61–63, with pp. 64–65 family/hierarchy context read in Wisconsin author-hosted scan text. General “all nations” formulations remain McClintock’s claims; no universal empirical certification or denial of women’s political action.

relations.relationship: Retains Said’s filiation/affiliation distinction while disputing a linear replacement of family relations by nonfamilial institutional orders.
relations.evidence_note: Specifically named primary response, printed p. 64 with pp. 63–65 context. She argues that familial images were reinvented within national and imperial institutions. Said’s underlying passage is not newly collated and the critique is not generalized to all his work.
